name: ytauto
summary: a youtube trend dashboard pairing a next.js frontend with a fastapi backend. server-side caching and an engagement proxy help compare candidate videos without claiming access to private retention data. automated video rendering is on the roadmap.
problem: Compare potential YouTube topics through a dashboard that gathers public video signals and scores candidates without pretending to know private audience-retention data.
highlights: Trend dashboard: Bring candidate videos and their public performance signals into a Next.js interface.
Engagement proxy: Combine view velocity, engagement rate, and an age penalty into a proxy score for comparing candidates.
Backend caching: Cache and aggregate requests on the server so the browser does not query YouTube directly.

media.caption: Content-planning interface before generation: title ideas, route mapping, and staged research.
In-app explanation of the analytics workflow and engagement proxy.

sections.heading: The workflow
sections.body:
- Retrieve and cache public video data.
- Filter candidates and calculate proxy scores.
- Compare candidates in the dashboard.
- Use the signals to guide further topic research.

sections.heading: Under the hood
sections.body: A Next.js frontend is paired with a FastAPI backend for ingestion, caching, and scoring. The repository separates analytics from future rendering work.

sections.heading: Scope & current state
sections.body: Trend analytics and proxy scoring are implemented. Historical storage, automated video rendering, and a mobile wrapper are roadmap items; the score is not an audience-retention measurement.
